findings.rationale: request.data -> requests.post(url, files = {"file":response.content}) in document_merge_service/api/views.py (line 52, 17 steps)
findings.title: untrusted_destination (model_entailed)

findings.rationale: self.groups = userinfo.get(settings.OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM) or []. Groups drive access control in views.py:25 (queryset.filter(group__in=self.request.user.groups)) and serializers.py:25. The claim is trusted verbatim from the userinfo response with no validation of issuer/audience, so any party able to influence that response controls group membership.
findings.title: Authorization groups taken directly from OIDC userinfo claim

findings.rationale: requests.get(settings.OIDC_USERINFO_ENDPOINT, verify=settings.OIDC_VERIFY_SSL, ...). OIDC_VERIFY_SSL is env-controlled (settings.py:193, default True). If set false, the bearer-token identity lookup accepts any TLS cert, allowing a MITM to forge userinfo (sub/groups) and thus impersonate users and gain group-based access.
findings.title: OIDC userinfo fetched with configurable SSL verification

findings.rationale: cache.get_or_set(f"authentication.userinfo.{hashsum_token}", userinfo_method, timeout=settings.OIDC_BEARER_TOKEN_REVALIDATION_TIME). OIDC_BEARER_TOKEN_REVALIDATION_TIME defaults to 0 (settings.py:197-198). A 0 timeout means the userinfo is not cached, forcing a network call per request; conversely a large value keeps revoked tokens valid. The cache key is a sha256 of the token, so cache contents are keyed by token hash.
findings.title: Bearer token cached by hash with configurable revalidation timeout

findings.rationale: return ENGINES[engine](template) indexes the ENGINES dict with the engine value. The engine comes from the template model/serializer (serializers.py:31-34, views.py:36). A KeyError on an unknown engine would surface as a 500 rather than a validation error; the value is constrained by model choices but the serializer path passes data.get("engine") before full validation.
findings.title: Engine dispatch via dict lookup on user-controlled engine value

findings.rationale: ("template", models.FileField(max_length=1024, upload_to="")) stores uploaded files directly in the media root with no subdirectory. Combined with the download view (views.py:66-84) which serves template.template.read() with a Content-Disposition attachment, uploaded filenames are not namespaced, raising collision/overwrite concerns.
findings.title: Template FileField with upload_to empty string

findings.rationale: if group and group not in request.user.groups: raise ValidationError. This is the write-side counterpart to the read-side filter in views.py:25. It relies on request.user.groups being trustworthy, which traces back to the unvalidated OIDC claim in authentication.py:32.
findings.title: Group assignment validated against request user's groups

findings.rationale: userinfo = {"sub": "1", settings.OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM: ["test"]} and the test asserts user.group == "test". The test confirms the implementation trusts the userinfo claim for group membership; no test covers issuer/audience verification or rejection of a mismatched token, so the trust boundary is untested.
findings.title: Auth test asserts group from mocked userinfo without issuer validation

findings.rationale: queryset.filter(group__in=self.request.user.groups) only applies when settings.GROUP_ACCESS_ONLY is true (default False, settings.py:190). When disabled, all templates are listed regardless of group. When enabled, AnonymousUser.groups is [] so filtering yields nothing, but the security posture hinges entirely on this env flag.
findings.title: Group-based queryset filtering depends on user.groups being populated

findings.rationale: requests.post(f"{settings.UNOCONV_URL}/unoconv/{convert}", files={"file": response.content}) sends the rendered document to an external conversion service. The convert value is validated against UNOCONV_ALLOWED_TYPES (serializers.py:52-58) and UNOCONV_URL must be configured, but the response content/status are passed straight back to the client (views.py:52-56), so the external service's output is trusted.
findings.title: Merge output forwarded to external UNOCONV_URL service

findings.rationale: TestUser(AnonymousUser) sets is_authenticated True and admin_client uses client.force_authenticate(user=admin_user). This is test-only scaffolding, but it means the group/authorization paths exercised in test_template.py never go through BearerTokenAuthentication, leaving the real auth boundary under-tested.
findings.title: TestUser bypasses real authentication for admin client

findings.rationale: SECRET_KEY = env.str("SECRET_KEY", default=default("uuuuuuuuuu")). The default() helper returns default_prod when ENV == "production", and ENV defaults to "production". So if SECRET_KEY is unset in production, the app silently uses the weak literal "uuuuuuuuuu" instead of failing. This is a predictable signing key for Django sessions/CSRF.
findings.title: Hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY in production default

findings.rationale: ALLOWED_HOSTS = env.list("ALLOWED_HOSTS", default=default(["*"])) — with ENV defaulting to production, the production default is ["*"], disabling Django host-header validation. Combined with DEBUG defaulting to False in prod, this permits arbitrary Host headers.
findings.title: ALLOWED_HOSTS defaults to wildcard in production
